This question is about finding a value for \(g\), the gravitational constant.
Consider the diagram below, showing a cube submerged beneath a column of liquid:

Diagram not to scale.


(a) The cube is experiencing a force of \({@if integerp(Fval) then Fval else float(Fval)@}N\) on its top face from the volume of liquid.
Find the pressure acting downwards on the cube due to the volume of liquid in \(kPa\).

[[input:ans1]] \(kPa\) [[validation:ans1]]

(2)

[[feedback:prt1]]

(b) The volume of liquid has a mass of \({@float(Mval/1000)@}t\).
Find the density of the liquid in \(kg/m^3\).

[[input:ans2]] \(kg/m^3\) [[validation:ans2]]

(2)

[[feedback:prt2]]

(c) Given the equation \(P = \rho g h\) where: \(\ P\) is pressure in \(Pa\)

\(\rho\) is density in \(kg/m^3\)

\(g\) is the gravitational constant in \(N/kg\)

\(h\) is the depth of the liquid in \(m\)


Calculate an experimental value for the gravitational constant.

[[input:ans3]] \(N/kg\) [[validation:ans3]]

(2)

[[feedback:prt3]]

Here is a worked solution:

The equation relating pressure, force and surface area is: \(P \ [Pa] = \frac{F \ [N]}{A \ [m^2]}\)

Using the values given:

\(P = \frac{{@Fval@}}{{@if integerp(Wval) then Wval else float(Wval)@} \times {@if integerp(Lval) then Lval else float(Lval)@}}\)

\(P = {@Fval/(Wval*Lval)@}Pa\)

\(P = {@float(Fval/(Wval*Lval*1000))@}kPa\)

You have used the right equation to relate pressure, force and surface area.
However, you have not converted the units of pressure into \(kPa\) correctly.
Remember, \(1kPa = 1000Pa\)

Here is a worked solution:

Rearranging the given equation for \(g\) gives: \(g \ [N/kg] = \frac{P \ [Pa]}{\rho \ [kg/m^3] \times h \ [m]}\)

Using the values obtained in parts (a) and (b):

\(g = \frac{{@float(Pval/1000)@} \times 1000}{{@RHOval@} \times {@Hval@}}\)

\(g = \frac{{@Pval@}}{{@RHOval*Hval@}}\)

\(g = {@Gval@}\)
